sections.heading: Questions about education
items: Can a school district buy through a cooperative?
For schools and government agencies, many Ramtech relocatable buildings are available through the purchasing cooperatives Ramtech is a vendor for. Ask which cooperative your district belongs to.

Can the building be moved later?
Relocatable buildings are designed for that. Permanent modular construction is designed to match the life expectancy of a site-built building.

sections.heading: About modular construction
items: Ramtech states that modular construction is usually 25 to 40 percent faster than site construction, because the foundation and the building are made at the same time.
Is modular as durable as site-built?
Ramtech states that modular buildings use the same materials and are built to the same codes as site construction, and last as long when maintained.
What does the no cost planning cover?
A floor plan, a site plan, an exterior rendering, outlined specifications and a preliminary budget, before any design fee.
Can we buy through a purchasing cooperative?
For schools and government agencies, many buildings are available through the cooperatives Ramtech is a vendor for, including BuyBoard and TIPS.
A full one-year written warranty from the date of occupancy on every new building Ramtech manufactures and installs in the continental U.S.
Controlled off-site factory production of engineered building sections, typically built 50 to 90 percent complete, then transported to the site, assembled and finished.
What is the difference between relocatable and permanent?

Both are made in the plant with the same materials as site-built structures. Relocatable buildings sit on a concrete block foundation and can be moved. Permanent buildings use a pier and beam or slab-on-grade foundation and site-applied finishes.
Can I finance a modular building?
Ramtech works with third-party finance companies, including finance leases, and can help you compare options.

pitch.heard_intro: Ramtech is a prospect, so nothing here comes from a conversation. Everything comes from ramtechmodular.com and the brief Quantum filled in. Tell us where it is wrong; your words outrank ours.
heard: The brief has no stated promise. The site's own headline is 'Ramtech is a design-build leader in modular building construction'; we used it, marked unconfirmed.
No likes, dislikes or ground preference were given. We chose the house light set.

Notes in the brief: design-build leader since 1982, direct manufacturer, more than 3,500 projects, the most modular buildings delivered to government, education, healthcare and commercial buyers in the Southwest.
The offer to lead with is no cost project planning and budgeting.
found: 829 URLs in the sitemap, 765 of them blog posts and image attachment pages. Average page score 44 of 100 (Quantum audit, November 2026).
No page title names a city. 517 pages are under 300 words, and only 2 carry FAQ markup.
Two figures disagree: the home page and Ramtech story say more than 3,500 projects; the Ramtech difference page says more than 4,000.
The site is open to AI crawlers (robots.txt allows them) but has no llms.txt file. The search and AI analysis for this domain has not been run, so no traffic figures appear here.
pitch.choose_intro: The words, the pages and the proof are identical in all three. What differs is the register. Open each one on your phone and tell us which feels like Ramtech.
choose_reasons: If a plain, procedural site is the argument
Clean: white ground, a humanist sans, hairline cards. Built for the facility manager, school business officer or procurement lead reading a page in order.
If a contemporary, confident look is the argument
Showcase: image-led, rounded, more sales-forward. Shows the buildings first.
Press: warm paper and a serif. Reads like the company that has been building since 1982.
pick_reasons: School districts, agencies and healthcare administrators comparing builders want the process, the contract routes and the proof on the page. Clean puts them first.
No cost planning, a firm fixed price, a one-year warranty, purchasing cooperatives: Clean lets each one sit in a plain list a buyer can check.
A 40-year-old builder that makes things should not look trendy. Clean is quiet enough for the buildings to be the subject.
pitch.pick_change: The Ramtech photographs are 2017 to 2019 and several are small. We would commission a current set of finished buildings before launch; the hero carries the whole page.
alternatives: The safe, sales-forward one: big building photographs, a wheel of the four markets, a drag comparison of site-built and modular sequences.
The wildcard: serif headlines on warm paper, the 1982 story high on the page. Nobody in modular construction looks like this.
plan: Choose a direction. Resolve the items under To confirm, starting with the promise and the project count.
Copy review with Ramtech: the project profiles, the floor plans library, and which blog posts are worth keeping.
Build in HubSpot: theme, templates, every page, forms routed to the right person at the plant.
Review rounds, a permanent redirect for every URL that exists today, QA on the same gate this preview passed.
Launch with the baseline captured the day before.
Measure against the baseline and decide the first articles from the questions buyers ask.

confirm: Who this is for. The brief says Ramtech is a prospect and lists Kelly Williams as a possible contact on our side, unconfirmed. Kelly Williams is named on Ramtech's own site as its Vice President of Business Development. Confirm who at Ramtech receives this.
The promise. The brief gives none. We used the home page headline, 'a design-build leader in modular building construction'.
The project count. The home page and the Ramtech story say more than 3,500; the Ramtech difference page says more than 4,000. We used 3,500.

Accent and header colour. The brief gives none. #cd2122 (red) is the most frequent colour in Ramtech's child theme stylesheet and matches the roofs in the photographs; #181818 is the header ground because the logo is white. Neither was checked against brand guidelines.
The logo is a white-type PNG fetched from the live site. Ask for the vector and a dark-type version.
Photographs are Ramtech's own, 2017 to 2019, taken from the live site. Which project is in which photograph is not captioned on the site, so alt text is descriptive only.

No written testimonials. The site features video narrations by Marty Crawford (West ISD) and Rev. John Wilke (Immanuel Lutheran Church and School), but no quoted text. Nothing is attributed to them here.
Named people. Ramtech's design team page names nobody, so no team section appears.
Mansfield coordinates (32.5632, -97.1417) are approximate, used only for schema markup.
The map section is left out because the map module has no Texas outline and Ramtech lists one location.
Financing and lease figures on the specialty pages come from Ramtech's procurement pages: confirm the $1 end-of-lease purchase and 100 percent financing still apply.
The SCIF page was only partly readable in our fetch; the standards named here are ICD-705 only.
The 31 Awards of Distinction, and 'since 1987', come from the awards page; confirm the current count.
No search or AI analysis was run, so there is no search package on the hub.
pitch.footer: Prepared for Ramtech Building Systems. Nothing here is live or indexed. Photographs are Ramtech's own, taken from ramtechmodular.com. Facts we could not source are listed under To confirm.
